Subject: Dedicated capacity help — quick context and ask

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Fontana is excited about moving some of our realtime summarization and conversational agents onto a dedicated pool. We need a pre-sales sizing worksheet so our infra folks can validate commit levels.

High level:
- Production target: ~2M monthly requests across API + web widgets (mix below).
- Current latency SLO target: p95 < 300ms for qps-bound endpoints, p99 < 1s during bursts.
- We have two main request types: short Q/A (avg 18 tokens prompt, 45 tokens response) and long summarization (avg 120 tokens prompt, 650 tokens response).

Can you send your dedicated sizing template and a short list of the traffic attributes you need (concurrency, session duration, warm cache assumptions, model variants, embedding %)? I can attach a small sample of our request logs.

Best,
Diane
Ops Lead, Fontana.ai

Hi Diane — great to meet yesterday and appreciate the sample. Attaching our Dedicated Sizing Template (redwood_dedicated_sizing_template.xlsx) — fill the highlighted tab and we can run a model-fit analysis.

Key fields we need (short checklist):
- Traffic volumes (RPS over time): typical and peak windows
- Concurrency distribution (active sessions, average and p95)
- Prompt/response token averages per route (you included these — please confirm by route)
- Session duration and session stickiness / affinity (KV cache hit expectations)
- Fraction of requests that call embeddings or repeated context (>0% matters for memory)
- Model family / size you expect to run and acceptable quantization (e.g., fp16 vs int8)
- Latency SLOs and burst duration tolerances (how long can p99 be > target)
- Any compliance/VPC constraints for Private vs Dedicated

We usually ask for a 7-day sample with minute-level RPS if available. Naomi and Karthik — will you review Fontana's CSV and flag any follow-ups?

Next steps: once the sheet is returned, we'll produce an initial GPU SKU map and expected committed capacity with burst cushion and cost estimate.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior AE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity help — a few technical clarifications

Hi Diane — quick follow-ups after skimming your CSV:

1) Session affinity: is the Q/A traffic stateless (each request independent) or do you maintain per-user KV context across multiple turns? If the latter, what's the average number of turns per session?

2) Cache warming: for summarization jobs, do you reuse a large context window (e.g., repeated system prompt + doc chunks), or are requests single-shot? That impacts KV cache size and memory per model instance.

3) Embeddings: you noted some metadata enrichment — can you give a percentage of total calls that are embedding requests and an average vector size (dimensionality)?

4) Model variants & fallback: do you plan to use multiple model classes (smaller for Q/A, larger for summarization) or a single model variant with different max lengths? Knowing split helps us recommend GPU mixing and automated routing policy.

5) Burst shape: your CSV shows a few short peaks — are those predictable (cron-like feeds) or user-driven spikes (unbounded)? Also, typical burst durations?

If you can reply inline in the sheet + drop one representative request sample per route (raw prompt + response token counts), that will let us calibrate p95/p99 token compute cost per request.

Thanks — Naomi (Solutions Eng)
From: Diane Park <diane@fontana.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity help — a few technical clarifications

Hi Naomi / Marissa — answers inline: 

1) Session affinity: Q/A is mostly stateless (single-shot) for public widgets. Internal agent flows keep context; average 3–4 turns per session for internal users only (~15% of Q/A traffic).

2) Cache warming: summarization reuses system prompt + doc chunks; ~80% of summarization requests reuse the same doc chunks across short bursts (so high KV cache hit). Typical context window pre-chunking = 8–12k tokens but we send ~2–3k per request after preprocessing.

3) Embeddings: ~12% of total calls are embeddings; vectors are 1536-dim.

4) Model variants: plan is smaller 7B-class for Q/A and 70B-class (quantized int8) for summarization. We expect about 70% of requests to be Q/A and 30% summarization by volume, but summarization is ~4x token-weighted.

5) Burst shape: user-driven (product launches & marketing campaigns). Peaks last ~15–40 minutes; largest peak last month was 22 minutes at ~6.5x baseline RPS.

Attached: updated sample CSV (trimmed) and a tiny prompt/response example for each route inside the sheet. Let us know if you need earlier retention windows (we have 30-day logs).

Thanks,
Diane
attachments: fontana_traffic_samples.csv (updated)

- Based on the embedding % and your 70/30 split, likely recommendation is a mixed pool: 2x 70B int8 pods for summarization with warm KV cache, and an autoscaled band of 7B-class instances for Q/A. We'll include a fallback routing policy to serve Q/A on cheaper instances when summarization bulk is low.
